column1: The COVID‑19 Inflation Weighting in Israel

The thesis titled The COVID-19 Inflation Weighting in Israel by Jonathan Benchimol  Itamar Caspi  and Yuval Levin  published in June 2022  examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on consumer spending patterns and inflation measurement in Israel. The authors highlight that the pandemic led to significant shifts in consumer behavior due to lockdowns and restrictions  which complicated the interpretation of official inflation data calculated by the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) using a fixed basket of goods. Israel  having experienced three lockdowns and a successful vaccination campaign  serves as the focus of this study.

The authors utilize credit card spending data to construct a synthetic consumption basket that reflects household consumption during the pandemic. This COVID-19-adjusted basket is then used to calculate an adjusted inflation rate for the pandemic period. The study finds that while there are differences between the COVID-19-adjusted and CBS (unadjusted) inflation measures  these differences are transitory. Notably  the contribution of certain goods and services  such as housing and transportation  to inflation changed significantly  particularly during the first and second lockdowns. Despite the significant bias in inflation weighting caused by lockdowns and restrictions in developed countries  the inflation bias in Israel during the COVID-19 period was unexpectedly small and transitory.

The thesis contributes to the broader discussion on substitution bias  which occurs when consumers switch to cheaper items over time  leading to an underestimation of inflation in standard consumer price indices. The authors reference previous studies  such as those by Braun and Lein (2021) and Jaravel and O’Connell (2020)  which discuss the variability of substitution bias under different economic conditions and the changes in consumer spending patterns during the pandemic. The study also notes that the CBS typically updates the Israeli Consumer Price Index (CPI) weights every two years based on the Household Expenditure Survey  but the fixed weights used during the pandemic did not accurately represent actual consumption patterns  leading to potential biases in inflation measurement.
The paper acknowledges the significant lifestyle changes and shifts in consumption habits caused by the pandemic  as documented by various studies (Chetty et al.  2020

The study uses data from Google Mobility Trends to illustrate the decline in movement to retail and recreation locations  which correlates with lower demand for nonessential goods and services. The pattern of changes in consumer behavior during the lockdowns in Israel is similar to that observed in other countries  with the first lockdown having the largest effect and the last one the smallest.

column1: The authors emphasize that the CBS's fixed consumption basket does not accurately represent the actual consumption basket during the COVID-19 period  leading to biased inflation calculations. By mid-January 2021  the number of COVID-19 cases and hospitalizations in Israel began to decline  aided by a rapid vaccination campaign. By the end of March 2021  a significant portion of the Israeli population had been vaccinated  allowing for the lifting of restrictions and a return to pre-pandemic consumption patterns.

In conclusion  the thesis provides valuable insights into the challenges of measuring inflation during periods of significant economic disruption  such as the COVID-19 pandemic. It underscores the importance of adjusting inflation measures to account for changes in consumer behavior and spending patterns to ensure accurate economic analysis and policy-making.
